column1: # protected-paths.tsv (harbor#1018) — the paths in harbor that only the operator may merge or deploy.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The operator's policy of 2026-10-06: a change touching one of these paths is merged or
# deployed only with the operator's approval, a click in Claude Code's own permission dialog; Claude merges and
# deploys anything else. The ship contract (§2) fixes the format and bin/gate-classify.sh reads it, for every repo
# that carries .agents/ship.conf. The policy, the settings lines and the residual risks: docs/design/approval-gate.md.
# FORMAT  glob <TAB> class <TAB> reason. Globs are repo-relative; `**` crosses directories, `*` and `?` do not.
# Always protected whatever this file says: this register, .agents/ship.conf and .github/**. A rename is judged on
# both of its paths and a deletion on the path it removes, so moving a file out of a glob, or into one, is protected.
# tests/gate/approval/classify.test.sh holds every hook-wired script and every installer to a row here.
# RECORDED TRADE-OFF. The suites the required checks run take their verdict from the PR's own tree. What decides
# which suites run and how they tally (contracts/suites*.txt, suite-paths.txt, ci-verified.sh, runners/**,
# tests/lib/**) is protected; the individual test files are NOT, because protecting tests/** would put nearly every
# PR behind the click. A PR can still weaken one test without asking: review a test diff, it is not gated here.
